title: SKHY Stock Slips Premarket After Korean Memory Giant Reveals $38B Expansion Plan Amid AI Hyperscaler Capex Frenzy
key_facts: SK Hynix said on Friday 2 Oct 2026 it will spend 54 trillion won (about $38 billion) expanding chip plants in South Korea, per Bloomberg.
Spending covers a new DRAM fab (Yongin Y2) and a NAND plant in Cheongju; about two-thirds goes to the DRAM project.
Yongin Y2 is the second of four planned fabs at the Yongin cluster; groundbreaking is planned for July 2027.
The stated aim is AI-driven memory demand, including high-speed DRAM and NAND storage.
Seoul shares closed down 4.9% on Friday; US-listed shares fell about 0.2% premarket; the company also said it will detail shareholder returns in Q3.
Context: SK Group, Samsung and the Korean government earlier pledged $880 billion for domestic manufacturing and AI; Korea aims to double memory capacity in five years.
SK Hynix Q2 revenue rose 257% year on year to 79.32 trillion won; it listed on Nasdaq on 10 July after raising $26.5 billion.
quote_evidence: SK Hynix said it will invest in a new DRAM fabrication facility in Yongin and a NAND manufacturing plant in Cheongju, with about two-thirds of the planned spending earmarked for the DRAM project, Bloomberg reported.
The new Yongin Y2 will be the second of four fabs planned at the Yongin semiconductor cluster, SK Hynix said, and the company intends to break ground on the project in July next year.
why_it_matters_hint: One of the two main suppliers of AI memory is committing $38 billion to new Korean fabs, with the bulk going to DRAM.
notes: Stocktwits is a copy site relaying Bloomberg; Bloomberg is the source. Original Bloomberg link not given; url is the Stocktwits page. Event was Friday 2 Oct, before the 3 Oct window, so marked follow-up and score lowered by 1.
